ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Prohibition of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism Offenses (Act No. 18970, as amended), Enforcement Decree thereof, Financial Transaction Reports Act (FTRA) under the Financial Intelligence Unit of the Financial Services Commission; Beneficial Ownership Reporting Regulations under the Commercial Act (Act No. 17905) and the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) guidelines; FATF Recommendations as implemented.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies of the foreign parent jurisdiction (e.g., Hong Kong Companies Registry, Singapore ACRA, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the original certificate in the country of issuance, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the competent apostille authority of the issuing jurisdiction; no consular legalization is required because the issuing jurisdiction is a member of the 1961 Hague Convention. Submit the apostilled certificate with a certified Korean translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of No Impediment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or equivalent corporate registrar of the foreign parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a fresh certificate from the relevant registry, then notarize and apply for a Hague Apostille in the issuing state; the apostilled document must be accompanied by a sworn Korean translation for filing with the Korean court registry and tax office.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the Korean resident director and attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company's board of directors or shareholder meeting
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified extract of the board resolution notarized in the foreign jurisdiction, then Hague Apostille; this path must not be combined with consular legalization. If the parent is located in a non-Hague state, a separate consular legalization chain through the Korean consulate is the exclusive alternative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation / Memorandum of Association of the Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies of the foreign parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of the foreign parent's constitutional documents, notarized and apostilled under the Hague Convention in the issuing state; Korean translation attached. For non-Hague jurisdictions, the certified copy must be authenticated by the Korean embassy and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing country, then submitted with the same Korean translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company's relationship bank (international banking department)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter is issued on bank letterhead and signed by an authorized officer; the bank's signature must be notarized, then the notarized letter must receive a Hague Apostille if the bank is located in a Hague member state. If the bank is in a non-Hague state, channel the letter through Korean consular legalization instead of combining both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Beneficial Ownership Registry Extract (where available in foreign parent's jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Beneficial Ownership Register administrator of the foreign parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Extract obtained from the official UBO register, notarized and apostilled in the issuing jurisdiction, accompanied by a certified Korean translation; where the foreign jurisdiction has no UBO register, a sworn ownership declaration with apostille is accepted by Korean court practice.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation, the foreign investor, its directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Korea's own Financial Sanctions List published by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any individual holds a prominent public position, has family or close associates who hold such positions, or where there is any unexplained source of funds. The compliance team must maintain a written risk assessment, perform perpetual screening at least every 15 days, conduct adverse media searches in Korean and the UBO's domestic languages, verify identity with government-issued documents, document source of wealth for any contributions above the statutory threshold, and file a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU within 24 hours of detecting a red flag. All records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hometax electronic filing system (www.hometax.go.kr) and the Supreme Court of Korea Company Registry (i-REG; www.iros.go.kr) name search portal, operated under the Commercial Act and the Act on Registration of Real Estate and Legal Persons
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Korean company name must be expressed in Korean script, including the requisite corporate form indicator 'Yuhan Hoesa' (유한회사). Any foreign-language brand name must be transliterated into Hangul according to the rules of the National Institute of Korean Language, and may also include an English alias name in parentheses if the Korean name is registered. The name clearance process requires a four-tier check: (1) exact Hangul match with existing registered names; (2) phonetic similarity likely to confuse ordinary persons; (3) identical corporate-form suffix; and (4) prohibited or misleading business-purpose tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the court registry system rejects a proposed corporate name, the applicant may submit a written objection to the registry office having territorial jurisdiction within two weeks of the rejection notice, attaching a comparative list of registered names, evidence of prior use of the mark, and a legal opinion if the rejection is based on clash with a similar existing name. The registry must review the objection and issue a written disposition; if the objection is again refused, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the competent district court within 60 days under the Administrative Litigation Act. During the appeal, the applicant may reserve a new fallback name by refiling the name reservation request in the i-REG portal. The entire objection and appeal procedure does not require legalization of foreign documents if the name issue is purely domestic, but any foreign evidence must be apostilled and translated into Korean.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office for a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in wholesale distribution of botanical products. The National Tax Service requires a physical place of management where books, corporate seals, and inventory records are kept, and where domestic personnel can receive tax notices and undergo field audits. Municipal registry authorities may reject a registered address that maps to a virtual office building or mail-forwarding suite. Banks handling Swift TT and wire transfers require evidence of a physical lease or owned premises, a fixed-line telephone, and a local corporate bank account opened with in-person verification. A shared administration-service physical suite of up to 25 square meters with a dedicated labeled office and secured filing cabinet may be tolerated if the registration documents show a full-time domestic administrator employed or retained by the company.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) municipal business registration certificate is posted visibly on the premises; (2) the company seal, registered corporate seal, and director identification are stored at the office; (3) import/export contracts and inventory records for goji berries and herbal botanicals are retained on site; (4) a local director or authorized employee is present during working hours; (5) the tax invoice records match the actual business location; (6) the lease is a bona fide lease, not a mail-forwarding contract. The quantified risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the National Tax Service or municipal registry within the first two years is 23 percent for the wholesale food industry, rising to 40 percent if the company claims export VAT refunds or zero-rated supplies in its first year. Educational site visits are possible during the opening of a corporate bank account and always when the business involves agricultural food imports or exports regulated by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Commercial Act and Court Fees Act, calculated on a standard nominal capital of KRW 10,000,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business registration certificate fee (National Tax Service local tax office) and corporate seal registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule for Business Registration Certificate and corporate seal certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary and competent apostille authority, plus translation agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of overseas notary fees, apostille processing fees, and Korean certified translation fees at USD 150-250 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hometax and i-REG name reservation and company registry record search package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court Company Registry Service Provider / Law Firm Firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for name clearance, UBO background check, and registry search performed by external counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance and PEP/sanctions screening fee for UBOs and foreign directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law Firm and third-party compliance database provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for initial sanctions list screening, adverse media search, UBO verification documentation, and File of compliance intake memorandum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for bank notarization, apostille, and sworn Korean translation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 4470, as amended), Chapter V concerning the Yuhan Hoesa (Articles 287-2 through 287-37), together with the general provisions on companies in Articles 54, 169 and 177, and the Framework Act on National Taxes, Article 168, regarding business registration and taxpayer legal identification.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section, Registry Office of the local District Court of the Republic of Korea (for example, Seoul Central District Court) having jurisdiction over the registered office of the company, administratively supervised by the Supreme Court Court Administration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Establishment Registration under the Commercial Registration Rules, together with the Certificate of Incorporation and certified registry extract issued by the District Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, before the establishment registration is filed, the initial contribution capital must be fully subscribed by the members and actually deposited into a designated Korean commercial bank account, and the bank issued deposit certificate must be attached to the registration filing. If any contribution is in kind, a court appointed examiner or certified appraiser must verify the specific property value. Once the company registration is completed, the deposited funds are available for ordinary business use and no further blocked escrow period is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This Pro-Forma First Board Resolution of the Yuhan Hoesa is adopted on the date set forth in the corporate minute book at the companys registered office by the unanimous consent of the initial members and the duly appointed board of directors. Whereas the company was established in the Republic of Korea under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea as a Yuhan Hoesa, and whereas the initial contribution capital has been fully subscribed by the members and the deposit certificate has been issued by the authorized bank, it is hereby resolved as follows. First, capital subscription and allotment. The board ratifies the statutory contribution subscription schedule filed with the registry, confirms the total initial contribution capital in KRW or equivalent foreign currency, and acknowledges that the liability of each member is limited to the amount of each members unpaid contribution to the extent required by law. The board directs the managing director to retain the capital deposit certificate in the corporate record book and to call any unpaid but subscribed contributions at any time upon 14 days prior written demand. Second, registered office adoption. The board approves the registered office located at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation within the Republic of Korea, authorizes the managing director to execute and deliver a lease or occupancy authorization, to file the registered office confirmation with the commercial registry, to notify the National Tax Service, and to display the statutory notices required for foreign trade operations. Third, banking authorization. The board authorizes the opening of corporate operating accounts, foreign currency export collection accounts, and SWIFT TT and wire transfer clearing accounts at the commercial bank selected by management. The board appoints the managing director and the financial officer as authorized signatories, requires two authorized signatures for all payments above USD 20,000, and permits one authorized signature for payments below that threshold. The board expressly approves the execution of banking mandates, beneficial ownership declarations, anti-money laundering questionnaires, and correspondent banking instructions for international bulk export transactions. Fourth, statutory officer appointments. The board appoints the managing director, the auditor, and the tax compliance officer identified in the incorporation schedule. The managing director is granted full day-to-day managerial authority to engage warehousing providers, to enter into international supply contracts, to open customs and export clearance accounts, and to file any licenses required for the wholesale distribution of dried botanical products. The auditor and tax compliance officer are directed to complete all regulatory filings, to maintain the statutory accounting records, and to supervise the timely submission of all export declarations and phytosanitary certifications. Fifth, common seal and execution clause. The board approves the corporate common seal and determines that all deeds, contracts, invoices, and customs documents of the company shall be signed by the managing director or a joint signatory and affixed with the corporate seal as required by Korean mercantile practice. Finally, this resolution is unconditional, binding upon all members, directors, and successors, and may be authenticated, apostilled, excerpted, and delivered to banks, ministries, foreign government agencies, and commercial counterparties as a certified extract of the first statutory board resolution of the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and contribution subscription schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public appointed under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea, with anticipated review by external corporate counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding members shall prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office address, precise business purpose covering the international bulk wholesale, export, storage, and distribution of dried goji berry, herbal botanicals, and related botanical food products, the aggregate amount of contribution capital, the contribution amount of each member, the method of contribution, the duration of the company, the number and powers of directors, the auditor provisions, and the accounting period. All founding members must execute the contribution subscription schedule by hand or by certified digital signature, and the execution must be witnessed by a notary public. The notary public shall verify the identities, passports, alien registration cards or corporate certificates of each founder, confirm the capacity and authority of each subscriber, and record the notarial certificate number on the Articles of Incorporation. The notarized Articles and subscription schedule form the foundational statutory instrument for the subsequent court registration, banking, tax, and licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation in Korean statutory form
Contribution subscription schedule executed by all founding members
Passport or alien registration card of each individual founder
Corporate certificate and power of attorney of each corporate founder
Notary public appointment request and fee payment receipt
Certificate of the corporate name availability or name validation statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to notarize because of an illegal purpose clause, missing capital subscription amount, or unclear in-kind contribution appraisal, the founders shall amend the Articles, reject the non-compliant clause, obtain a new contribution schedule, and resubmit the instrument to the same or another notary within one business day. If the notary requires an apostille or certified translation of a foreign founders passport, the founder shall immediately obtain the apostilled copy from the Korean consulate or from the competent ministry in the founders country.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the capital contribution deposit account and obtaining the bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial banking institution in the Republic of Korea, including major Korean banks with corporate banking and foreign exchange dealing capabilities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding members shall approach the selected Korean bank with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the contribution subscription schedule, proof of the registered office address, founder identification, and the tax identification or alien registration number of each founder. The bank shall open a provisional capital subscription account in the name of the future company or, if permitted by the bank, a domestic value account linked to the future corporate entity. Each member must transfer his, her, or its subscribed contribution into this account by wire transfer or direct deposit, and the bank shall issue a certificate confirming receipt of the full amount of initial contribution capital. If the contribution is made in foreign currency, the bank shall record the transaction in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and issue a certificate of inward remittance. In-kind contributions must be evaluated by the court-appointed examiner or a certified appraiser, and that report must be made available to the bank and the registry. The bank deposit certificate must bear the bank seal and date no earlier than one day before filing for establishment registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscription schedule and member identification documents
Application for corporate provisional account opening
Beneficial ownership declaration and anti-money laundering questionnaire
Foreign exchange transaction declaration or inward remittance evidence
Lease contract or address evidence for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to open the account because an incorporator is not a Korean resident, the incorporator shall obtain an Alien Registration Card or, where no domestic address exists, an approved certified identification from a foreign bank together with a Korea Securities Depository or foreign exchange declaration. If the bank questions the source of funds, submit signed sale contracts, promissory notes, or audited financial statements proving legitimate origin. If the bank still refuses, the founders may change the deposit bank and re-open the account within two business days using a foreign investor dedicated branch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Company Establishment Registration with the competent District Court commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section, Registry Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the Yuhan Hoesa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The statutory representative shall file the Application for Company Establishment Registration with the commercial registry division using the official court forms. The application shall be accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank deposit certificate, the contribution subscription schedule, the consent or appointment documents of each director and auditor, the directors identification, a certificate of the corporate common seal, a report on the registered office address and, if in-kind contribution is used, the court-appointed examiners report. The application must also include the original lease contract for the registered office, proof of payment of the registration tax and local education surcharge, and the court fee stamp. The registry examiner will verify that the company name is not identical to an already registered enterprise, that the business purpose is lawful, that the officer eligibility requirements are met, and that the paid-in contribution is genuine. Upon approval, the court issues the corporate registry abstract and assigns the unique registration number. The company comes into existence as a legal person on that registration date.
required_dossiers: Application for Company Establishment Registration in official court form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and the notarial certificate
Bank deposit certificate for the full initial contributed capital
Contribution subscription schedule and members register
Consent forms and appointment resolutions for directors and auditor
Lease contract and landlord consent certificate for the registered office
Certificate of the corporate common seal and seal impression
Proof of payment of registration tax, local education tax, and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a request for supplementation because of missing signatures, unclear address evidence, or incomplete officer information, the applicant shall file the corrected document and payment receipt within the court-prescribed period, usually seven to fourteen days. If the registration is refused, the founders shall determine the ground of refusal, amend the Articles or documents, and re-file as a corrected original application. An administrative objection or judicial remedy may be sought through the competent court where the refusal involves a question of law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service and export trader filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Tax Office of the National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea serving the district where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one calendar month after the company establishment registration is completed, the managing director shall apply for a Business Registration Certificate using the corporate taxpayer application process through the National Tax Service electronic portal or in person at the local regional tax office. The application shall state the company name, corporate registry number, registered office, representative director, purpose of business, business establishment date, and the main business code corresponding to wholesale trade and export of food and beverage products. The tax officer will verify the physical existence of the office, the identity of the representative, and the corporate registration certificate. Upon issuance of the Business Registration Certificate, the company shall obtain an electronic tax invoice authentication code and register for Value-Added Tax, Corporate Tax, withholding tax, and, if required, for the status of an export business. The Tax Service will also synchronize the corporate number with customs, allowing the entity to file electronic customs export declarations and obtain export clearance.
required_dossiers: Corporate registry abstract issued by the District Court
Certificate of the corporate seal impression and representatives identification
Business Registration application form executed by the managing director
Lease contract or real property use certificate for the registered office
Article of Association or statement of business purpose
Corporate bank account deposit certificate or proof of capital payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service holds the Business Registration application because the business purpose is considered speculative or because the address is a virtual office, the company shall present a physical office inspection, a signed lease, utility bills, and warehouse or storage contracts to prove substantive business presence. If the suspension is based on a director ineligible to act on tax matters, replace the tax compliance officer and file a corrected officer notification. Re-application may be submitted electronically immediately after the cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the operational corporate and export collection banking account and completing statutory social insurance registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank selected by the board and, for social insurance, the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance system, and the Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service under the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Business Registration Certificate is issued, the managing director shall present the corporate registry abstract, the Business Registration Certificate, the corporate seal certificate, the board resolution, the passport or alien registration card of each authorized signatory, and the beneficial ownership statement to the selected bank. The bank shall conduct customer due diligence and verify the business purpose as international wholesale of dried botanicals and herbal food products; it shall open a corporate current account, a foreign currency export account, and a wire transfer account with SWIFT TT capability. The bank will issue correspondent bank instructions and confirm foreign currency collection terms. Once the bank accounts are opened, the company must register with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance system, and the Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service as a new employer, and file any required list of covered persons with the local employment and labor office. The managing director must also post the workplace safety notice and appoint a safety and health supervisor if employees are hired.
required_dossiers: Corporate registry abstract issued by the court
Business Registration Certificate issued by the National Tax Service
Certificate of corporate seal impression
First board resolution authorizing banking signatories
Beneficial ownership declarations and anti-money laundering questionnaire of all directors
Contracts or purchase orders supporting the international export business
Social insurance registration forms of the employer and employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank declines account opening because of an adverse anti-money laundering determination or incomplete address verification, the company shall supply the final corporate registry extract, the signed first board resolution, the underlying export contracts, and a source-of-funds statement. If the refusal persists, submit the dossier to another licensed commercial bank using its foreign investor assistance desk. For social insurance rejections, correct the employee list or the employer identification and file the corrective form on the day of receipt.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) of the Republic of Korea, the local Si, Gun, or Gu district office responsible for the business premises, the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency for phytosanitary certification, and the National Agricultural Products Quality Management Service for organic certification claims.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Retail and Wholesale Business Report under Article 36 of the Food Sanitation Act, Food Export Declaration Certificate for each export lot, optional Organic Processed Food Certificate for organic marketing claims, and phytosanitary certificate issued by the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency where the importing country requires plant health status verification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea through the Korea Environment Corporation, and the local Si, Gun, or Gu environmental department overseeing the specific site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III, meaning Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for a normal dried botanical wholesale, repacking, and low-rise storage operation. A prior environmental review or full EIA report is triggered only if the project involves new construction of a warehouse, logistics center, or processing facility with a cumulative gross floor area of at least 20,000 square meters, or development within an environmental protection, water source protection, or military cultural protection zone. For ordinary leased or existing wholesale warehouse premises, only environmental registration and compliance with general waste, sewage, and fire safety obligations are required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater is generated by the wholesale and packaging of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals. Domestic sewage shall be discharged into the public sewer in accordance with the local sewer ordinance, generally requiring biochemical oxygen demand not exceeding 300 mg/L for municipal sewer entry; if an individual private sewage treatment facility is used, the effluent standard shall comply with Water Environment Conservation Act limits, including BOD not exceeding 10 mg/L, SS not exceeding 10 mg/L, pH maintained between 5.8 and 8.6, and total nitrogen within permit limits. No volatile organic compounds, heavy metals, or hazardous air pollutants are introduced by the process. If botanicals are handled in bulk, airborne organic dust shall be controlled by local exhaust ventilation so that occupational exposure remains below 5 mg/m3 respirable dust and no visible fugitive opacity crosses the site boundary. Any waste is classified as non-hazardous food waste and municipal waste, and shall be removed by an approved waste carrier unless composted or recycled under Ministry of Environment regulations. If phosphine or other fumigant chemicals are used for pest control, the company shall first register the fumigant with the Rural Development Administration or MFDS and comply with the enforced Korean Occupational Safety and Health Agency exposure limits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises shall obtain the fire protection system completion inspection certificate from the local fire department under the Fire Services Act, including approval of automatic fire alarms, portable fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and evacuation routes. If the warehouse floor area exceeds 16,000 square meters, the operator must register as a special fire safety management object, conduct a fire and evacuation drill at least once a year, and submit the annual self-fire inspection report. The building use permit must authorize storage and wholesale occupancy, and any structural racking or mezzanine must be approved by the local district office for structural load capacity. The business must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act by appointing a workplace safety and health manager, conducting new-hire and annual safety training, and filing the industrial accident compensation insurance registration and the manifest of dangerous machinery and equipment with the Ministry of Employment and Labor. Civil defense authorities must be notified if the space is used as a designated emergency evacuation shelter or if any hazardous chemical storage threshold is exceeded; ordinary dried botanical storage below the designated threshold is not subject to additional civil defense licensing.

stage_2.sla_and_remedy_notes: The total statutory formation cycle is approximately 19 business days, assuming a single member structure, no court supplementation, and no environmental EIA trigger. All adverse administrative actions may be cured within the courts or agencies prescribed statutory cure period; government portals provide electronic resubmission for tax and customs filings.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), operating the HomeTax e-Tax portal (www.hometax.go.kr); cross-border export clearance and customs supervision are handled by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS portal (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that commences a taxable business or establishes a domestic place of business in South Korea must file a Business Registration Application with the competent district tax office, or through the HomeTax online portal, within 20 days of business commencement. For non-resident entities with no Korean address, the application must be accompanied by a Power of Attorney appointing a tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes, an apostilled certificate of incorporation, board resolution authorizing the Korean business activity, evidence of the fixed domestic place of business, and identification of the responsible representative. On acceptance, the NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number that serves as both the corporate TIN and VAT ID. This registration is mandatory for domestic exporters: the locally incorporated Yuhan Hoesa, as a Korean-resident exporter, obtains its own corporate Tax Identification Number and VAT registration through this business registration procedure and must separately be registered in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa; a domestic incorporated entity is always classified as a separate corporate income taxpayer. Korean law applies hybrid mismatch rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act, but no elective pass-through or hybrid entity classification is available. Qualifying domestic groups may elect consolidated corporate tax filing, but this statutory consolidation does not change the entity-level taxation classification of each subsidiary.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no monetary VAT registration threshold for a Yuhan Hoesa: mandatory VAT registration is triggered by the first taxable supply or the opening of a business in South Korea, regardless of turnover. The KRW 80 million annual turnover threshold applies only to the simplified taxpayer regime for individual sole proprietors and is not available to corporate entities. Even export-only turnover requires VAT registration because only a registered VAT taxpayer can issue valid tax invoices, file periodic VAT returns, and claim the 0% export VAT rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea does not operate a Latin-American-style real-time fiscal clearance system with server-side digital stamping. Instead, the NTS enforces a mandatory electronic tax invoice regime: registered VAT taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices through the HomeTax electronic tax invoice system or an NTS-approved open API-integrated ERP system, and transmit the data to the NTS by the day following the date of issue. The NTS validates invoices electronically for duplicates, mismatches, and fraud patterns, and for B2C supplies retail sellers must issue electronic cash receipts where payment is made without a tax invoice. Export declarations must be cleared electronically through the KCS UNI-PASS system, which records the outward movement of goods and is the anti-fraud backbone for zero-rated export VAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies mandatorily to exported goods, including dried goji berries and herbal botanicals supplied in the ordinary export trade, under Article 24 of the VAT Act. The statutory requirements are that the seller is a registered Korean VAT taxpayer, the goods physically depart the Republic of Korea, and the export is evidenced by a customs export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service. A domestic delivery to a foreign buyer, or a sale where the goods do not actually leave Korea, is standard-rated at 10%. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to non-resident customers and used wholly outside Korea may also be zero-rated, but the present goods export derives its 0% treatment from the physical export declaration rather than an e-service rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry) accepted by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the international carrier evidencing physical export
Commercial Invoice and Packing List describing the dried goji berries and herbal botanicals
International Sales Contract / Purchase Order executed with the overseas buyer
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, evidencing receipt of export proceeds
UNI-PASS export clearance result data confirming the outgoing cargo movement and customs release
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly verify the export declaration, bill of lading, cargo tracking, foreign exchange settlement, and the identity of the offshore purchaser. If zero-rating is claimed without genuine physical exportation, or if documents are false, the NTS will retroactively claw back the 0% rate and assess the 10% VAT, plus statutory additional tax, collection interest, and overdue penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Willful misconduct can be prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment of up to three years and fines up to three times the evaded tax. The Korea Customs Service may additionally impose smuggling or false-declaration customs penalties up to a multiple of the evaded customs duty, and the exporter must retain all supporting export, customs, transport, and foreign exchange documents for at least five years after the VAT filing due date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) – Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, jointly administered with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime and has achieved full current-account convertibility; most trade-related and service-related transfers are unrestricted and can be executed through designated foreign exchange banks without prior approval. Capital-account operations, however, including foreign direct investment, equity subscription, cross-border loans, and certain portfolio transactions, remain subject to notification, reporting, or approval under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, as administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and monitored by the Bank of Korea. A foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa can open Korean won and foreign currency accounts and may receive capital contributions in USD or KRW after filing an initial foreign-investment report with a Korean foreign exchange bank; foreign currency borrowing beyond statutory thresholds must be reported to the Bank of Korea or the relevant regulatory authority. Export proceeds are generally received and retained in foreign currency within a designated foreign exchange account, and conversion to Korean won is at market rates without automatic compulsory surrender, but reporting violations can trigger administrative penalties. Profit repatriation is permitted after certified financial statements are issued, the final foreign-investment report is filed, and corporate income tax obligations are settled; however, dividend remittance can be delayed by documentation checks and requirement to prove that the original capital entry was properly registered and that the underlying earnings originated from bona fide trade receipts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must collect export proceeds within 15 months from the date of exportation; extensions are possible for unavoidable causes with approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the Bank of Korea. There is no mandatory conversion ratio, meaning exporters are not forced to convert foreign currency into Korean won; however, once received, 100% of export foreign currency proceeds must be credited to a designated foreign exchange bank account or converted into Korean won through a licensed bank, and the receipt must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEBIS).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Current Account (Korean Won) plus Foreign Currency Trade Receivables Account
Primary Operational Settlement Account with designated USD Receivables Sub-Account
Capital Injection / Foreign Direct Investment Custodial Account plus Operational Won Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Exchange Export Proceeds Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Global digital EMIs and offshore electronic money institutions are not licensed to hold deposits or maintain domestic corporate current accounts in South Korea. Financial operations require a banking license under the Banking Act or Express Money Transfer Business license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and foreign EMIs generally cannot provide the statutory foreign-exchange bank relationship needed for Korean trade settlement, capital verification, FEBIS reporting, or profit repatriation. A Yuhan Hoesa should use a tier-one domestic commercial bank for all corporate treasury activity; fintech EMIs may be used only as ancillary payment initiation tools where the underlying liquidity stays in a licensed Korean bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For first-time corporate account onboarding of a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory statutory representative and at least one authorised signatory must appear physically in-branch at the Korean bank. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a standalone KYC method; however, a notarised and apostilled power of attorney may permit a resident domestic director or contact officer to complete day-to-day banking actions after the original overseas representative has been identified in an in-person interview at the Korean bank or one of its overseas branches. The bank will require the corporate seal certificate, corporate registration certificate, business registration certificate, certified copy of the consolidated Minutes of Board resolution, valid passports or Alien Registration Cards, and proof of the final beneficial owner's identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and multi-tier ownership through an offshore intermediate create an incomplete beneficial-ownership trail, with the bank unable to confirm senior management and natural-person controllers above 25%.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified incorporation certificates and register of shareholders for every intermediate legal entity up to natural-person level; group structure diagram; notarised and apostilled passport or national ID of each ultimate beneficial owner; signed UBO declaration; audited or shadow financial statements of the parent; bank reference letters; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation such as tax returns, investment statements, or sale contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The declared ISIC 4631 dried-goji-berry and herbal wholesale scope conflicts with expected transaction size, invoice frequency, counterparty geography, or value of each remittance, which may indicate trade-based money laundering or invoice manipulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed export sales contracts and purchase orders; export customs declarations; phytosanitary certificates or organic certification; warehouse receipts and inventory records; bills of lading or airway bills; freight forwarder billing; invoice and packing list alignment; last six months of supplier and buyer bank statements evidencing trade-flow consistency; final customer-end price schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border remittance counterparty screening flags an enhanced-maintained jurisdiction, restricted person, or transshipment hub, creating concern that herbal botanicals could be re-exported to a sanctioned destination or converted into a shell logistics chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and adverse-media screening report over the entire counterparty chain; UN, EU, UK OFAC, US OFAC, and Korean SDQ screening logs; end-user declaration; consignee corporate certification; pollicy statement confirming no re-export to sanctioned states; detailed routing and transshipment explanation; export permits; import permits from the destination country if available; customs valuation records matching the shipping documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company has zero domestic banking footprint, minimal Korean payroll or tax filing history, and paid-in capital that appears small relative to the announced cross-border trade pipeline, raising doubt on the authenticity of the equity contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Initial foreign-investment declaration filing receipt; FEBIS or bank-generated inward remittance confirmation; certified capital verification report issued by a Korean certified public accountant; paid-in capital ledger and canceled deposit slips; resolution of the shareholders' meeting approving capital contribution; certificate of incorporation with paid-in capital reflected; lease agreement for storage or warehouse; purchase orders from customers; and evidence of operational readiness such as health-use compliance and tax registration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all inward equity and shareholder loan transfers in USD, EUR, or KRW via SWIFT to the Yuhan Hoesa's designated foreign-exchange bank account under the direct investment purpose code for a Korean foreign-invested company. The foreign investor must file the initial foreign-investment report with the receiving Korean foreign-exchange bank or through the Foreign Exchange Information System before or at the time of remittance; bank-level recognition of the report number is required for the wire to be classified as legally admitted capital rather than personal transfer. After the inward remittance is credited, the receiving bank confirms the payment, and a Korean certified public accountant issues the paid-in capital verification certificate confirming the share issuance or capital increase. This packaged documentation must be filed at the Korean court registry and tax office; no third-party depositor or unrelated account can act as the capital originator for a foreign-invested entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Export disbursements and trade settlements for dried goji berries and herbal botanicals should use SWIFT MT103 for ordinary telegraphic transfers from the buyer, or documentary collection with the Korean bank forwarding the sight or term draft, commercial invoice, packing list, insurance certificate, phytosanitary certificate, and transport documents. Where a buyer's country requires a letter of credit, the Korean bank can negotiate export bills under an at-sight or usance LC subject to complete documentary compliance; proceeds are credited to the foreign currency settlement account and may then be converted to Korean won or retained subject to FEBIS reporting. All outbound third-party supplier payments must carry proper purpose-of-payment codes and be supported by domestic supply contracts to prevent misclassification of trade vs. capital outflows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla USD/KRW forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank, limited to projected export trade receivables or import payables and typically available to maturity of up to 12 months upon presentation of trade documents or receivable due inventory
KPW NDF-style hedge coverage for cross-currency mismatch if the underlying receivable is in a non-deliverable currency, with FEBIS-reporting and no speculative open position

Cross-currency swap facilities for a Yuhan Hoesa only where the entity has matching external trade borrowing or foreign currency liabilities; the swap must be supported by an exposure statement, board resolution, and underlying debt or trade contract

Currency option or collar structures permitted as a risk-stripping overlay with premium and strike terms fully disclosed to the Korean bank, subject to the bank's internal suitability and the corporate treasury hedging policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return including balance sheet, income statement, deferred tax schedules and related-party disclosures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer: on or before March 31 of the year following the tax year, i.e. within three months after the fiscal year-end; an authorized one-month extension to April 30 is available for book-closing or external-audit-linked corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax, 40% for intentional concealment; late payment accrues a daily 0.022% surcharge from the day after the due date; continued non-payment permits NTS asset seizure and auction, and an inactive delinquent K Company may be administratively struck off from the commercial registry court register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Corporate Income Tax Return for the local surcharge on national corporation tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government where the head office is located, filed through the NTS unified electronic filing interface and the local tax information system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer: on or before April 30 of the year following the tax year, i.e. within four months after the fiscal year-end, subject to the applicable local-tax extension rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local corporate income tax triggers a 20% non-reporting penalty, a daily 0.022% late-payment surcharge, enforced collection by seizure of bank accounts and tax clearance refusal, which in turn blocks banking export payment rails and can lead to administrative deregistration of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Certified External Auditor Report and audited Korean statutory financial statements under the Korean External Audit Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) under the external-audit report system; the audited financial statements must also be presented to the ordinary meeting of members and attached to the NTS corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If a mandatory audit threshold is triggered, the external auditor must be appointed within four months after fiscal year-end, the audit report delivered to the general meeting of members within six months after fiscal year-end, and the report transmitted to the FSS within the statutory filing window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing fee applies; however, failure to appoint or retain a certified auditor when legally required is subject to administrative fines of up to KRW 20,000,000; false audit certification or balance-sheet falsification carries criminal penalties and may result in compulsory strike-off from the corporate register by the registry court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Report and Beneficial Ownership declaration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, when any non-resident owns 10% or more of member equity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) using the integrated foreign investment management system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the close of the fiscal year; any foreign equity acquisition, transfer, or shareholding change must be reported separately within 30 days from the transaction date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual report or a 30-day beneficial-ownership change report may incur a penalty of up to KRW 20,000,000, loss of foreign-invested enterprise tax refunds and incentives, and a mandatory corrective order; continued noncompliance can support NTS and registry action to declare the entity inactive and strike it off the commercial register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa, being a limited liability company, must appoint an independent certified public accountant to perform a statutory audit if, at the end of the fiscal year, its total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,300,000); or if it meets at least two of the following three criteria: (i) total assets of KRW 10,000,000,000 or more (approximately USD 7,700,000); (ii) annual revenue of KRW 30,000,000,000 or more (approximately USD 23,000,000); (iii) an average of 300 or more employees during the fiscal year. An audit is also required where the Korean External Audit Act, the Financial Services Commission, or a specific statutory designation classifies the entity as public-interest relevant, and any audit report must state compliance with mandatory audit procedures and accounting standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for corporations subject to external audit and for publicly accountable entities; a small non-listed Yuhan Hoesa below the audit thresholds may prepare its statutory financial statements under K-GAAP or applicable Korean small- and medium-corporation accounting standards, provided corporate income tax bases are computed under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Commercial Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the Yuhan Hoesa must maintain an accurate beneficial ownership and member register. Any resident transfer of a member interest must be recorded in the Register of Members without undue delay and in all cases within 30 days of the transfer; any non-resident acquisition, transfer, or disposal of 10% or more of member ownership must be filed with MOTIE through KOTRA within 30 days. Annually, when submitting the NTS corporate tax return, the company must complete the beneficial-owner questionnaire and related information. Although Korea does not maintain a general public UBO register for private LLCs, bank and AML/KYC documentation supporting Swift/TT and wire-transfer payment rails must be reconfirmed at least on a rolling basis and no later than upon any material change in members, directors, or beneficial owners. An annual UBO confirmation memorandum signed by all members must be placed before the ordinary general meeting and retained for at least seven years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Officers including any statutory auditor appointed
Register of Charges/Mortgages over corporate assets
Minute Book of General Meetings of Members and Board of Directors meetings
Share certificate issuance and surrender register where member certificates are used

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 3,500 per year for a Korean registered office and company secretarial agent, depending on city and service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 30,000 per year for a certified K-IFRS statutory audit, including travel, tax reconciliation, and register audit, for an export-oriented wholesale dried goji berry and herbal botanical exporter

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea applies progressive corporate tax rates under the Corporate Income Tax Act (CITA): 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 22% on income between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion; 25% on income exceeding KRW 300 billion. Additional local surtax (local income tax) of 10% of the corporate tax payable applies. Tax incentives for agriculture, forestry, and fishery businesses, including dried goji berry herbal wholesale, may include deductions for special tax credit for increased employment, investment tax credits, and R&D tax credits. The tax loss carryforward period is generally 10 years for losses incurred from 2018 onwards, but up to 15 years for losses of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) under certain conditions. Free trade zone or foreign investment zone incentives may be available only if the entity qualifies as a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준및세액계산서) Form No. 30 (for the head office) filed via HomeTax (홈택스) electronic filing system (www.hometax.go.kr); supplementary schedules under the Corporate Tax Law Enforcement Decree.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year-end based: within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, deadline is March 31 of the following year); a 1-month extension is available for foreign-invested companies or where the tax return is prepared by a licensed tax accountant (extended to 4 months after year-end). Quarterly estimated corporate tax prepayments are due within 3 months of the fiscal quarter for corporations with prior-year taxable income exceeding a statutory threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, business registration number, representative director, head office address, fiscal year commencement and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean entity identifier (e.g., KR_YUHANGHOESA) and its domestic business registration number (사업자등록번호). The foreign parent or beneficial owner must be listed in the supplementary 'Foreign Shareholder' schedule; failure to disclose ultimate foreign shareholders may trigger anti-money laundering scrutiny and tax information exchange reporting under the Common Reporting Standard (CRS).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code, standard industrial classification (ISIC 4631 / Korean KSIC 46312), and detailed description of the wholesale trade of dried goji berries, herbal botanicals, and related products.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that the Korean KSIC code and business scope reflect the actual cross-border wholesale export model. If the Korean company purchases dried goji berries from domestic farms and resells to foreign buyers, the trade activity must be clearly documented as wholesale trading. Misclassification may lead to recharacterization as a broker or service provider and unwarranted transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (법인세 과세표준 계산 / Corporate Tax Base Computation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue (매출액), cost of goods sold, selling and administrative expenses, non-taxable income (익금불산입), and non-deductible expenses (손금불산입).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border export sales, revenue must be recognized per the Korean tax law accrual principle and transaction currency conversion rules using the Bank of Korea base exchange rate. Expenses paid to offshore affiliates must be scrutinized for arm's length substantiation; undocumented management fees or royalty payments to a related foreign entity are automatically disallowed as deductible expenses under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (세액공제 및 감면 / Tax Credits and Exemptions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reductions such as foreign tax credits, investment tax credits, job creation credits, and special tax exemptions for agricultural/forestry/herbal wholesale entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign tax credit (FTC) may be claimed on foreign-source income, but only by submitting the Foreign Tax Credit calculation schedule (별지 제17호 서식) with certified evidence of foreign tax paid. No unilateral tax credit can exceed the Korean corporate income tax attributable to the foreign-source income. If the offshore customer is a related party, withholding taxes imposed by the customer's jurisdiction may not be creditable without a valid tax treaty residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly estimated corporation tax prepayments, withheld tax amounts, and taxes paid at source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that all prepayments made by the Korean entity equal the amounts uploaded in HomeTax. Overpayment may create a refundable audit trail; underpayment triggers 3.03% per-month interest arrears (0.03% daily surcharge) and additional 50% negligence penalty for under-reporting tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (차가감 세액 및 납부세액 / Net Tax Payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable, local income tax surcharge (10% of corporate tax), interest and negligence penalties, and amount remitted to the tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders receiving dividends, Box 6 must be reconciled with the withholding declaration requirement of the withholding agent. Dividends declared but not actually repatriated are still subject to withholding tax at the moment of the dividend resolution or actual payment, whichever occurs earlier. The tax officer will cross-check Box 6 against the (former) withholding tax return (원천세 신고) under the Income Tax Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 20% of the unreported (evaded) tax as a negligence penalty, plus an additional 0.6% per day up to a maximum of 75 days for understated tax. Failure to file without tax underpayment: KRW 200,000 to KRW 1,000,000 per case. Failure to submit transfer pricing documentation: penalty up to KRW 30 million (or 2% of the adjusted income) and 100% additional assessment for false documentation. Criminal fraud thresholds: intentional evasion exceeding KRW 500 million in tax is punishable by imprisonment up to 2 years; evasion by a corporation may trigger a dual fine and liability for the representative director under Article 18 of the Tax Evasion Punishment Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (statutory rate under the Income Tax Act Article 156(1)(d) for non-residents; effective rate becomes 27.5% including 10% local income tax surcharge on the withholding amount).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced 0% or 5% withholding tax under the Korea–Country Tax Treaty (e.g., Korea–U.S. Treaty Article 10, or Korea–Singapore / Korea–Germany / applicable bilateral DTA): (1) The foreign recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its competent tax authority, covering the calendar year of the payment; (2) The recipient must submit Form 갑지21호 (Dividend Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction Application) or the 'Application for Tax Treaty Benefit' (귀속법인용 세액면제신청서) to the Korean withholding agent before payment; (3) A beneficial ownership declaration must be completed, confirming the recipient is not a pass-through or conduit arrangement and has substantive economic activity; (4) The Korean payer must file the application with the district tax office within 9 months from the end of the month in which the dividend was paid; (5) Retroactive refund is possible only within 3 years (or 5 years for foreign-investment exceptions); failure to file voids the treaty benefit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% (plus 2.5% local surtax); treaty rate commonly 5% to 15% (e.g., 5% for Germany or U.S. under certain conditions, 15% for others) depending on the intellectual property type and beneficial ownership; Interest: statutory 25% (plus 2.5% local surtax); treaty rate commonly 10% (e.g., 10% under most Korean DTAs; 0% for interest on public bonds or government loans under some treaties). Thin capitalization rules: interest paid to a foreign controlling shareholder exceeding 2 : 1 debt-to-equity ratio (or 6 : 1 for financial institutions) is non-deductible and may be recharacterized as dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.5 million) of intercompany transactions with foreign related parties per fiscal year triggers Local Files and Master File preparation; KRW 5 billion threshold requires submission of a Local File summary; KRW 10 billion threshold also triggers a Master File submission. In addition, a 'Controlled Foreign Corporation (CFC)' rule applies to Korean companies holding more than 50% in a foreign subsidiary located in a low-tax jurisdiction (effective tax rate below 15%).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA) Articles 5 and 6 apply the arm's length principle and substance-over-form doctrine. The Korean entity must demonstrate a real principal-agent relationship, actual employees, premises, inventory, and decision-making capacity for its herbal wholesale export activities. Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) equivalent are enforced through the OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) minimum standards; if the Korean entity is a pure pass-through or acts only as a 'booking vehicle' for a foreign parent, the National Tax Service (NTS) may recharacterize income, deny treaty benefits, and impose a 10% additional penalty on the understated income under Article 76-5 of the Framework Act on National Taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Willful Deficit in Corporate Income Tax Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a corporate income tax return with intentionally understated export revenue, fabricated purchase invoices for dried goji berry procurement, or unauthorized deduction of management fees payable to a related Hong Kong or foreign entity without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3(1): imprisonment up to 2 years (aggravated up to 5 years if evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million) or fine up to 3 times the evaded amount; plus the National Tax Service imposes 40% of the understated tax as a negligence penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 48(2), and 0.66% monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 39(1), the director may be jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unpaid tax if the director grossly neglected duties. Civil asset restitution includes seizure and sale of personal bank accounts, vehicles, and real estate. Criminal criminal proceedings: travel ban (출국금지) under Article 26 of the Tax-Related punishment procedures; obstruction of a tax officer may lead to imprisonment. The corporate veil is pierced where the corporation was used as a shell for tax fraud; the representative director and any financial officer physically signing the fraudulent return face criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years and personal restitution for all penalized tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misdeclaration and Thin Capitalization Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dried goji berry inventory to a related foreign distributor at an artificially low price (non-arm's length) while paying inflated royalty or interest to the foreign parent, or maintaining a debt-to-equity ratio exceeding 2:1 with offshore shareholders, thereby eroding the Korean tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: LCITA Articles 4–6: NTS makes a transfer pricing adjustment equal to the arm's length price; grossly unfaithful transfer pricing documents may attract a penalty of KRW 30 million or 2% of the adjusted income. Interest on the unpaid tax accrues at 0.66% per month; additionally, a 10% penalty for inappropriate intercompany transactions may be imposed. Thin capitalization recharacterization: deductible interest denied and treated as constructive dividend subject to withholding tax of 25% plus surtax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for tax assessments arising from transfer pricing adjustments if they signed the transfer pricing documentation or the corporate return without reasonable cause. The NTS may issue an asset preservation writ (압류), a travel ban, and a criminal referral for 'fraudulent evasion' if the price manipulation was deliberate. The court may uphold unlimited personal restitution and disqualification from serving as director for up to 5 years under the Commercial Act Article 622 (unlawful conduct by directors).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance Facilitating Tax Treaty Abuse or AML Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a pass-through entity for dried goji berry sales: no employees, no warehouse, no local management; invoice routing to foreign jurisdictions; misleading declaration to claim DTA withholding tax relief for a shareholder who is not the beneficial owner; failure to comply with the Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act or failed AML beneficial-ownership filing under the Financial Transactions Report Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Framework Act on National Taxes Article 76-5 permits outright denial of treaty benefits; the National Tax Service may assess additional corporate income tax, 20% negligence penalty, and withhold tax at 25% (plus 2.5% surtax) on disguised distributions. The Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) can impose a fine up to KRW 100 million for failure to report beneficial ownership, and the CFC rule under LCITA Article 28 may attribute offshore profits. Violations of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for cross-border payments without a full declaration are subject to a fine up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow shareholders of a Korean shell company are jointly and severally liable under the Commercial Act Article 623 for actions performed in the company's name. Piercing the corporate veil: court may send the corporate assets into receivership and impose personal civil restitution for dividends deemed repatriated abroad. Criminal liability: imprisonment up to 3 years for foreign exchange violations, and up to 5 years under the Act on Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes if the economic loss exceeds KRW 5 billion. Travel bans are routinely issued to prevent directors from leaving the country during active NTS investigations; passports of foreign directors may be revoked via international letters rogatory.
